skill: Identify every true triangularity statement by inspecting the correct off-diagonal half of a square matrix, transposing and, for the hard family, adding or subtracting the transpose.
reasoning_steps: Read the matrix and each independently phrased statement.
Form the indicated transpose or sum/difference when applicable.
Upper triangular means every entry strictly below the diagonal is zero; lower means every entry strictly above is zero.
Select all and only true statements; None of the above is true exactly when all substantive statements are false.
response_contract: Stored practice uses one Boolean checkbox per statement, with a complete true/false choice bank. Canonical example expresses I/II/III verbally but has no captured answer-field bank; do not invent its original bank.
difficulty: Moderate captured instances use A, A^T and three statements on 3x3 or 4x4 matrices. Hard adds transpose sums/differences. One sum instance has no recorded difficulty.
invariants: Square matrices; diagonal entries do not determine triangularity.
Retain zero-testing, transpose and observed +/- operations, Boolean select-all response and comparable workload.
Diagonal matrices qualify as both upper and lower; transpose swaps the halves.
permitted_variations: Vary label independently of truth, signed integer entries including diagonal zeros, sparse nonzero positions, and 3x3/4x4 size.
Vary which off-diagonal half has nonzeros: lower-only, upper-only, both, neither. This changes qualifying statements and selection counts and is essential eligible answer-bearing variation.
Vary transpose target upper/lower and statement order independently of label and matrix profile.
Within hard scope vary symmetry/antisymmetry of mirrored entries so sums/differences may cancel or not; do not fix the derived statement true just because a source example does.
essential_vs_incidental: The all-zero tested half and exact transpose arithmetic are essential. Particular A/B/C/D labels, fixed diagonal entries, lower-only profiles, correct counts and option positions are incidental assignments, not constraints.
source_refs: tutorial 658a47dc-4d32-5d9d-a04c-82d683e87739: upper triangular is square with all entries below the diagonal zero; lower uses above; any number including 0 is allowed on diagonal and other half.
canonical 205d32a2-ac26-5eaf-896a-c6182a70eff7: A lower true, upper and A^T-A lower false.
prerequisite e3d1f202-a3d6-561f-bd4b-3e886142e5a0: interchange rows and columns.

lesson_passages.passage: An **upper triangular** matrix is a square matrix in which all entries *below* the diagonal are zeros.
Note that we can have any number (including $0$) on the diagonal and above.
A **lower triangular** matrix is a square matrix in which all entries *above* the diagonal are zeros.
